source.source_text: FACTUAL RECORD: Mike Tyson was born in Brooklyn, New York, on June 30, 1966. Teenager: met Bobby Stewart, a counselor and former boxer; Stewart introduced Tyson to trainer Cus D’Amato. D’Amato became Tyson’s coach and legal guardian. Tyson won Junior Olympic gold medals in 1981 and 1982. Professional debut: March 6, 1985; first 19 professional bouts were knockout wins. D’Amato died on November 4, 1985, before Tyson won a world heavyweight title. On November 22, 1986, Tyson defeated Trevor Berbick for the WBC heavyweight title at age 20, becoming boxing’s youngest heavyweight champion at the time. In 1987 Tyson won the WBA title and defeated Tony Tucker to unify the WBC, WBA, and IBF titles. James “Buster” Douglas gave Tyson his first professional loss in Tokyo in 1990. In 1992 Tyson was convicted of rape in Indiana, received a prison sentence, and was released on parole in 1995. He returned to boxing, regained the WBC and WBA titles in 1996, then lost the WBA title to Evander Holyfield later that year. In their 1997 rematch Tyson was disqualified after biting Holyfield’s ears; Nevada’s commission revoked his boxing license and later restored it. Lennox Lewis knocked Tyson out in 2002. Reported end-of-2005 record: 50 wins, 6 losses, 2 no contests, 44 knockouts. Muhammad Ali, Sugar Ray Robinson, and Joe Frazier are boxing-history context only, not Tyson opponents or coaches.
